explanations.text:
The skill claude reads when you give an abstraction and want the code under it.

  you: "/human an http server using python that returns hello world"
       the tool registers the project first — the file list, the reader,
       the empty project map — so there is a place for your words before
       there is any code                                           ([the skill](human))
       claude hands your words to the project map as they are: no spelling
       fixed, no word trimmed, no pin; the entry is flagged as yours and
       keeps that first copy as its origin
       claude writes the code files, no comments; the gate is static like a
       compiler's — the file must parse — and there is no run and no test
       claude maps the detailed telling of each file, in a shape from the
       catalog beside this skill — the rail by default          ([the shape](The rail shape))
       claude hands your words back with pins in them, through a plain
       retext; the gate strips the pins and compares the rest with the words
       it holds, character for character — one changed character is a
       refusal, so the pins go in and your words do not move
       when the project has more than one file, claude maps one more telling
       of the project — what you can ask for and which file answers each part
       claude reports each file and the project, and gives you the reader
                                                                      ([the run](The run))

  you: "I would say it differently"
       your new words go in with --verbatim, pins and all; the origin is reset
       to them, and the entries that stood on the old words are marked stale

  you: change the code yourself, then "sync"
       claude rewords your abstraction only where the code forces it — the
       smallest edit, in your voice — and the tool warns you with the changed
       lines; the origin stays in the map, show marks the entry against it,
       and a retext --verbatim with the origin brings your words back

  the pins tie a few words to a block, an earlier entry, another file, or an
  entry of another file's map; unique words, real targets, no circle, the
  detailed entry before the plainer one                              ([the pins](Pins))

  afterwards: sync runs exactly once per change, then once more for the
  project map, and with --stale when a file's entry made your abstraction
  wrong; an abstraction mapped before the flag existed takes the flag with
  a retext of its own text                                          ([the rules](Rules))
